title: Super-Logarithmic Entanglement Scaling in a Monitored Superconducting Chain
abstract: We develop a Keldysh-replica non-linear sigma model (NLSM) for the entanglement dynamics of a monitored one-dimensional spinful $s$-wave BCS chain in the rare-measurement regime, $γ\ll J,Δ$. Although the clean spinful $s$-wave BCS Hamiltonian belongs to symmetry class CI, spin-resolved measurements and projection to a conserved $f$-sector reduce the effective problem to class C. Starting from the corresponding parent symplectic saddle, we show that measurement backaction and the pairing amplitude impose complementary mass constraints that gap out different fluctuation channels. Their interplay dynamically projects the surviving massless modes onto an $\textrm{SO(R)}$ target manifold in replica space. A one-loop renormalization group analysis of this $\textrm{SO(R)}$ NLSM shows that, in the replica limit $R\to1$, the beta function becomes negative, producing a weak-anti-localization flow. This flow yields a super-logarithmic steady-state entanglement scaling $S(L)\sim \ln^2 L$ in the rare-measurement regime. Our field-theoretic result explains the numerical evidence reported in the companion Letter [arXiv:2604.04375] and shows that a topologically trivial monitored $s$-wave superconductor can realize an $\textrm{SO(R)}$ weak-anti-localizing critical phase without relying on a Wess-Zumino-Witten term.
summary: This work develops an effective field theory description using the Keldysh-replica NLSM for entanglement dynamics in a monitored BCS superconductor. By analyzing the RG flow of this model, the authors predict that the system settles into a critical phase characterized by super-logarithmic entanglement scaling ($\ln^2 L$). This result explains numerical findings without invoking topological terms.
main_problem: The study investigates entanglement dynamics in a monitored superconducting chain, focusing on characterizing the critical phase established by the interplay between unitary evolution and projective measurements.
main_result: The system exhibits super-logarithmic steady-state entanglement scaling, $S(L) \sim \ln^2 L$, driven by a weak-anti-localization flow in the effective field theory description.
method: The analysis employs the Keldysh-replica non-linear sigma model (NLSM) formalism combined with one-loop renormalization group (RG) calculations to analyze the low-energy fluctuations.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional spinful s-wave BCS chain subjected to rare, spin-resolved projective measurements ($\gamma \ll J, \Delta$). The effective dynamics are mapped onto an SO(R) target manifold in replica space.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy scaling $S_s(L)$, and the running coupling constant $g(\ell)$ derived from RG flow.
important_parameters: Rare-measurement regime ($\gamma \ll J, \Delta$), Replica limit ($R	o 1$), and the system size $L$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a rare-measurement limit and relies on projecting fluctuations onto an SO(R) manifold after applying saddle point approximations.

paper_structure: The paper develops the Keldysh-replica NLSM for entanglement dynamics. It analyzes how measurement backaction constrains the system to an SO(R) manifold. Finally, a one-loop RG analysis of this model yields the super-logarithmic scaling result.
why_interesting: It provides a field-theoretic understanding of non-equilibrium steady states in superconducting systems under continuous monitoring, linking concepts from critical phenomena (RG flow) to quantum information measures (entanglement entropy).
